\(P(A\vert{}B) = \frac{P(B\vert{}A) \times P(A)}{P(B)}\),
P(A|B) (Posterior): The probability that event A is true after considering the new evidence 
B.P(B|A) (Likelihood): The probability of seeing evidence B if event A is true.
P(A) (Prior): The initial probability of event A before new evidence.
P(B) (Marginal): The total probability of seeing the evidence B across all possibilities
